title: Zipf-aware KV cache compression probe: hybrid lossy formats and runtime fallbacks
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Purpose: Probe a Zipf-aware compression strategy for the KV cache that chooses between hybrid lossy formats (FP8/INT8/INT4 blocks) and full-precision FP16 storage at runtime, guided by token frequency and batch patterns. Goal is to quantify memory savings, tail latency impact during continuous batching, and generation quality degradation across realistic workloads. This ticket documents the experiment plan, datasets, measurement harness, early results, and proposed fallback policies for production rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end experiment harness that can switch storage formats per KV block and simulate continuous batching workloads
Quantified memory reduction vs FP16 baseline across three models and three workload mixes
Measured quality delta (next-token accuracy, logprob KL, and aggregated human-like scoring proxy) with thresholds defined for safe fallback
Runtime fallback policy prototype that triggers dequantization or pinning when quality degradation or latency regressions are observed
Clear runbook with metrics to monitor if rolled out to Dedicated or Private deployments
experimental_plan: 1) Implement an on-device KV block manager that partitions KV cache into 256-token-aligned blocks and stores each block in one of: FP16, FP8 (E4M3-like), INT8 symmetric, INT4 block-coded. 2) Implement a Zipf estimator that tracks per-key/token frequency over a sliding 10k token window and assigns a "hotness" score. 3) Compression policy: hot blocks -> FP16 or FP8; warm -> INT8 with per-block scale; cold -> INT4 with block-quantized codebooks + residuals optionally stored. 4) Run offline sweep across three workloads (conversational, web-search prompts, code-completion) and three models (Llama2-13B, Mistral-7B-v0.2, and an internal 30B staged replica). 5) Measure memory footprint, per-request p95 latency under continuous batching simulation (arrival process trace), and quality metrics. 6) Evaluate hybrid runtime fallback: if a block causes >X drop in logprob or an end-to-end quality regression on a small verification prompt set, dynamically rehydrate that block to FP16 for the next N requests.
datasets: web-search-sim-100k: anonymized user prompt traces sampled from hosted API (binned by length and context reuse)
conv-15k: multi-turn chat eval set with reference continuations (synth+human)
code-10k: developer prompts for code completion (varied lengths)
random-prefix-stress: artificially generated long-context sequences (to stress KV growth)
metrics: memory_reduction_percent: overall GPU KV cache memory reduction vs FP16 baseline
next_token_accuracy: top-1 match versus baseline generation
logprob_kl: KL divergence of token logprobs between compressed and FP16 runs
p95_latency_ms: per-request p95 under continuous batching (trace-driven)
allocation_fragmentation: measured GPU allocator fragmentation when blocks are rehydrated
dequant_cpu_overhead_ms: extra CPU cycles/time for dequantization operations
recovery_rate: fraction of blocks successfully rehydrated after fallback triggers
end2end_quality_proxy: composite score combining perplexity delta and an automatic semantic-similarity metric
results_summary: Early runs (Llama2-13B, conv workload) show: INT8 block storage yields ~44% KV memory reduction with median next-token accuracy drop of 0.8% and logprob KL of 0.035; FP8 yields ~28% reduction with 0.3% accuracy drop; block INT4 with single-codebook shows ~62% reduction but accuracy drop >4% on long-context verification prompts. Continuous-batching trace tests reveal p95 latency increase of 12-18ms for on-demand dequantization at burst sizes >32 when hot blocks are rehydrated frequently. Hybrid policy (hot->FP8, warm->INT8, cold->INT4-with-residuals) hit a Pareto point at ~40% reduction with <1% accuracy loss and p95 latency impact <8ms when using amortized lazy dequantization and a pin cache for frequently rehydrated blocks.
observations: Zipf distribution: token frequency skew correlates strongly with dynamic hotness; a small fraction of KV blocks (top 12%) account for ~65% of accesses in conv workload
Dequantization burst cost: rehydrating many warmed-up blocks in a single batch leads to allocator contention and fragmentation at high batch sizes
Residuals matter: storing a small FP16 residual per block for INT4 quant dramatically reduces quality loss with modest memory overhead (~6% extra), recommended for code workloads
Per-block adaptivity: using a micro-history (last 500 accesses) to choose storage format performs better than static frequency thresholds
Verification subset: small validation prompt set of ~200 canonical prompts is effective at early detection of harmful quality regressions when evaluating candidate compression states
decisions: Adopt hybrid per-block policy in experiment harness: hot->FP8, warm->INT8, cold->INT4+residuals
Implement pinned-dehydration LRU: maintain a small pinned FP16 pool (configurable percent of KV memory) for frequently rehydrated blocks to avoid churn
Expose two new runtime knobs to customers: kv_compression_profile (off|conservative|balanced|aggressive) and kv_pin_pool_size (0-20%)
Add automated quality gating: if end2end_quality_proxy drops >1.5% for a tenant during A/B, automatically rollback compression for that tenant
next_steps: Build production-grade allocator-aware rehydration module that preallocates scratch buffers to reduce fragmentation
Run long-duration A/B on low-risk tenants with 'balanced' profile for 2 weeks and collect rollout dashboards
Implement fast path SIMD kernels for INT8->FP16 dequant on GPU to reduce dequant_cpu_overhead_ms
Add a lighter-weight online Zipf sketch (count-min + decay) to keep memory for hotness estimator under fixed budget
Draft runbook and alerting rules (rt-alerts) for 'rapid rehydrate' events and quality drifting
